title: Army service and return to New Orleans, Floyd Hunt
summary: After the 1943 records Zardis went into the Army for three years, returned about 1946, played at Mississippi City and joined Floyd Hunt in Denver.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well, that's more money. Yeah, it was money. After you made those records with George in 1943, didn't you go into the Navy or something like that?
Right after that. That's right. That's correct.
Where did you get back to New Orleans?

Well, I stayed in the Army. I got in, it was about three years I stayed over there. And I got back around here around forty-six. I'll be a little before forty-six, but in that three years' time, you know.
Yeah. Did you play much then when you got back?

Yes, I played a whole lot when I got back, because when I first got back, this man of Gabriel, know that I got back and he came to my house and seen me, asked me if I wanted to work with him. He had a regular job playing at Mississippi City. That's, you know, I don't know if you know where that's at. That's way on the other side of, well, that's way away from Covington. But it's, I mean, it's a different route, you know what I mean? Well, anyhow, I played with him a long time over there, so, and that's the a long time, which was about a month. Then I got a, I got a telegram from Denver, Colorado, by a guy by the name of Floyd Hunt. He had a combo over there. Well, how he knew it, my name, I didn't know. He must have got it from the union. Well, all right, he sent me a telegram asking me if I wanted to join his band. And they were paying, oh, 175 hours a week. So, I asked at that telegram and told him that I was ready to come on out there, you know? So, after the boys in the band, Manna Gabriel and Hubert Moran, say, man, I wouldn't go out there if I was you, because if you're playing with some guys, you don't know. I said, let's don't know where you're going to get to know if you go to different places. So, I left about a week after, and I went out to Denver, Colorado, in a giant Floyd Hunts band. Well, he had a combo, you know? But he had a nice combo, too, really nice. So, they liked it, the way I played, and I stood with them a long time.
